question: What Is Choked Flow in a Control Valve?
body_html:
Choked flow in a control valve is a condition where flow stops increasing even though downstream pressure keeps falling. In liquids it comes from cavitation or flashing when vena contracta pressure drops below vapor pressure. In gases it occurs when velocity reaches sonic speed at the vena contracta.

Below this limit, liquid flow follows Q = Cv × √((P1 − P2) / Gf). Example: Cv = 10, P1 − P2 = 16 psi and Gf = 1 give Q = 10 × 4 = 40 gpm.
